sentences.text:
Writ Petition No.7702 Of 2023
 Order:

The writ petition is filed seeking following relief:
"......to issue an order or direction more particularly one in the nature of writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ declaring the action of the respondent No. 3 in interfering in civil disputes and threatening the petitioner and his family members that they shall not insist the respondents No 4 to 7 for vacating them from the leased premises and not taking any action against the respondent Nos. 4 to 7 even though the FIR No.112 of 2023 was registered on 02.02.2023 for the offences of cognizable and non bailable is nothing but arbitrary, illegal, null and void and violative of principles of natural justice and also violative of Articles 14, 19 and 21 of the Constitution of India.

Consequently, direct respondent No. 3 not to threaten the petitioner and his family members that they shall not insist the respondent No. 4 to vacate him from the leased premises and not to interfere in civil disputes thereby take necessary action against the respondent Nos. 4 to 7 basing on the FIR No.112 of 2023,
dated 02.02.2023 ......"
2.
The petitioner claims to be the owner of house bearing No.1-7-1/3, admeasuring 665 sq. yards situated at Boduppal Village and Municipality.

It is the contention of the petitioner that his father entered into a lease agreement with respondent No.4 and a registered lease deed was executed vide document No.11397 of 2017 and as per the terms of the lease respondent No.4 has to pay the rent of Rs.27,000/- per month.
The lease deed executed by the petitioner's father and respondent No.4 expired in the month of August, 2018.
But, respondent No.4 instead of complying the lease conditions is avoiding to vacate the premises.

It is the further contention of the petitioner that when his wife and his father went to the said premises and requested respondent No.4 to vacate the premises, respondent No.4 with the assistance of respondent Nos.5 to 7, manhandled his wife and father and have threatened them with dire consequences.

In this regard, the petitioner filed a complaint against respondent No.4 on the file of respondent No.2, but no action has been initiated by the respondents-Police, therefore, he was constrained to file a complaint before the IV Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar.

entities.text: IV Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Ranga Reddy District at
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The said Court after examining the complaint referred the same to respondent No.3 for registration of crime, upon which respondent No.3 registered a case vide F.I.R No.112 of 2023 against the unofficial respondents for the offences punishable under Sections 327, 341, 417, 420, 506 and 509 read with 34 of I.P.C and the same is pending for investigation.

sentences.text: The grievance of the petitioner is that at the instigation of respondent Nos.4 to 7, respondent No.3-Police are calling the petitioner to the police station and insisting him to withdraw the complaint and forcing him to enter into compromise with respondent Nos.4 to 7.
Hence, this writ petition.

4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home submits that a complaint has been filed by respondent Nos.4 to 7 against the petitioner and as the said complaint revealed cognizable offences,
after conducting preliminary enquiry, the respondents-Police have registered a crime which is pending for investigation.

He further submits that the petitioner was summoned for the purpose of investigation into the case vide F.I.R.No.112 of 2023 and the respondents-Police have not interfered with the civil disputes between the petitioner and respondent Nos.4 to 7 in any manner.

5. In view of the above submissions, the writ petition is disposed of directing the respondents -Police not to interfere with the civil disputes between the petitioner and respondent Nos.4 to 7, in any manner, except in accordance with law.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.

C.V. BHASKAR REDDY, J July 21, 2023 SUS S. Sudhakar vs The State Of Telangana And 6 Others on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99203375/
